pages.intro: `MfxClient` signs every request with your Ed25519 key, retries a rate-limited read after the platform's own `Retry-After`, never retries a write, and opens the stream. Each area of the API is a property of the client (`client.Terminals`, `client.Execution` and so on). A `Secret` or a `SigningKey` prints as `***`.

types.name: ExactDecimalConverter
types.doc:
A `Decimal` as the API writes it: a JSON string such as `"1.10450"`, read and written exactly.

A JSON number token is refused where the contract says string, because a number has already passed through binary floating point in whatever wrote it: `0.1 + 0.2` is not `0.3`, and a price that is one ulp off is a different price. The scale is kept, so `"1.10"` round-trips as `"1.10"`. An exponent, a thousands separator or a currency sign is refused.

A password travels through the caller's code, this SDK and an HTTP request, past string interpolation, loggers and exception messages. Revealing it takes the one explicit call that is easy to see in review.

types.name: Signing
types.doc:
The four headers every MFX Hub request carries, and the exact message their signature covers.

A request is signed, not bearing a token. `X-MFX-Key` names the key. `X-MFX-Timestamp` and `X-MFX-Nonce` make each request usable once. `X-MFX-Signature` is the base64 Ed25519 signature over `timestamp_ms\nnonce\nMETHOD\npath_with_query\nsha256_hex(body)`.

The timestamp is epoch milliseconds and must be within 30 s of the platform's clock. The nonce must be unique per key for five minutes. It is inside the signature, and it is one line of the signed message, so it is restricted to `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$`: a nonce with a newline in it could move the line boundaries and sign one request as another. A retry is therefore a new signature, never the same one sent twice.

members.doc: The header naming the key.

members.name: TimestampHeader
members.doc: The header carrying the request's time, in epoch milliseconds.

members.name: NonceHeader
members.doc: The header carrying the request's single-use nonce.

members.name: SignatureHeader
members.doc: The header carrying the base64 Ed25519 signature.

members.name: Message
members.signature: public static byte[] Message(string timestamp, string nonce, string method, string pathWithQuery, ReadOnlySpan<byte> body)
members.doc: The exact bytes an MFX Hub signature covers. One place, so the client and its tests agree.

raises.doc: The nonce is not 16 to 64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`. It is refused here rather than sent, because the platform answers a bad nonce with 401, which says nothing about why.

types.name: SigningKey
types.doc:
A tenant's Ed25519 private key. It renders as `***` wherever it could be printed, and it is never serialised.

The platform returns the private key once, when the key is issued, and never stores it. This type never writes it anywhere: `SigningKey.ToString` is `***`, and serialising it with System.Text.Json throws.

members.name: FromSeed
members.doc: A key from its 32 raw private bytes.

members.name: Parse
members.doc: A key from its PEM (PKCS #8) form, or from the base64 of its 32 raw bytes.

raises.doc: The text is neither, or is a key of another kind.

members.name: Sign
members.doc: The base64 Ed25519 signature of `message`.

members.name: PublicKey
members.doc: The 32-byte public key, which the platform holds to verify signatures.

types.name: Terminals
types.doc:
This tenant's terminals (`client.Terminals`): ask for one, submit the login that makes it real, watch it reach ACTIVE, restart, drain, resume and retire it.

Every write takes the caller's idempotency key and has no default: the point of the key is that the caller can retry with the same one and get the same answer back rather than a second terminal. A credential is a [Secret](#client.Secret), never printed.

members.name: OnItsWay
members.doc: The states a terminal passes through on its way to ACTIVE; every other state is settled.

members.name: OperationFinal
members.doc: An operation is over in any of these states; every other state is on its way.

members.name: OfflineIsTemporary
members.doc: OFFLINE needs nothing from the caller: the platform brings the terminal back when its host reports again, or moves it to another host of its farm. Retrying a request against an OFFLINE terminal is right; re-creating the terminal is not.

members.name: IsUsable
members.doc: Can this terminal be used right now, for market data, execution and account reads? True only in ACTIVE: every other state is not yet, not any more, not until resumed, or not at the moment (OFFLINE, FAILED). Checking through this means a state the platform adds later cannot read as usable.

pages.intro: Order entry (`client.Execution`). Every method returns an `ExecutionResult` and none throws for an outcome: a timeout, a transport fault and a broker rejection are all results with a reason. Prices and volumes are `decimal`.

types.name: Execution
types.doc:
Order entry for one tenant's terminals (`client.Execution`). Every method returns an [ExecutionResult](#execution.ExecutionResult) and none throws for an outcome.

A transport fault, a timeout, a rate limit, a refusal and a broker rejection are all outcomes of trying to trade, and a caller that must catch each one to learn whether it has a position will eventually place two. Execution is asynchronous: the platform answers 202 with a command id once the command is persisted, and the outcome arrives on the stream or from [GetCommandAsync](#execution.Execution.GetCommandAsync); [WaitForAsync](#execution.Execution.WaitForAsync) polls until the command is final. The idempotency key is required and has no default; nothing is retried automatically, not a timeout, not a rate limit, not a 5xx. A price, volume or distance is a `Decimal`: a `Double` does not convert to one implicitly, so a binary float never reaches the wire. What is refused before sending (a blank key, a negative decimal, nothing to modify) throws `ArgumentException`: that is the caller's mistake, not an outcome.

The whole answer to one execution call. Never thrown: always returned.

types.name: MfxStream
types.signature: public sealed class MfxStream : IAsyncDisposable, IAsyncEnumerable<StreamEvent>
types.doc:
The multiplexed stream: ticks, candles, events and results on one signed WebSocket.

A reconnect resumes what can be resumed and counts the rest: events, results, account and expert channels carry a per-channel `seq` and are resumed from the last one seen; ticks and candles subscribe again, and their gap is counted rather than hidden.

Nothing is buffered on the caller's behalf: a read takes the next frame from the socket, so a slow consumer meets real backpressure and is closed by the platform with 4008, which is counted. Close code 4001 (re-authenticate) throws [AuthException](#errors.AuthException): every reconnect would meet the same wall, and a client spinning on a revoked key looks like an outage.

types.name: Risk
types.doc:
Risk Management (`client.Risk`): account rules, the trade planner, exit plans and challenges. The rules, thresholds and actions are the tenant's; MFX Hub runs them on the account's own numbers and says what it did and why.

Bodies (rules, resets, steps, orders, a preview) are given as the generated models or as anything that serialises to the contract's shape (a `JsonObject`, a dictionary, an anonymous object); a decimal goes as exact text, and a binary floating-point number anywhere in one is refused before anything is sent. A new entry that breaks a rule in force is refused with [RiskRefusedException](#errors.RiskRefusedException), whose [RiskRefusedException.Refusal](#errors.RiskRefusedException.Refusal) names the rule, the figure used, its limit and what the entry would have made it. Several values of a filter go as repeated parameters.

types.name: Copy
types.doc:
Copy Trading for this key's tenant (`client.Copy`): leaders, followers, groups, stop-outs, requested closes, signals and the copy log.

One of the tenant's accounts, or an external signal source, leads; other accounts follow it, each with its own scaling, bounds, symbol map, options and limits. The tenant chooses them; MFX Hub executes and suggests none. Reads need `copy:read` and writes `copy:write`; every write takes the caller's idempotency key and is sent once. A nested setting (`scaling`, `bounds`, `options`, `risk_limits`, `filters`, `copies`, `limits`, `who_may_join`, `template`, a preview's rows) is the generated model or anything in the contract's own names (`new { mode = "fixed_multiplier", multiplier = 0.5m }`): a decimal goes as text, a `Double` anywhere is refused, and a name the contract does not have or a word outside its list is refused, all before anything is sent. A list page is the contract's page model with its `stats` row, counted over everything the filters match; an `All...` method follows the cursor.

members.name: RefusalReasons
members.doc: Why a copy did not fill: the contract's closed list, in its order. `broker` comes with the venue's code beside it.

types.name: BillingPaymentRequiredException
types.doc:
402 `billing_payment_required`: a payment is missing on the billing profile the request falls under, and nothing was done. Not retryable: sending the same request again changes nothing until the payment is made.

At [Stage](#errors.BillingPaymentRequiredException.Stage) `reminder` it comes only from a request that adds something billed; once `suspended` it can come from any write on the tenant or the profile, whatever route it was sent to. Reads keep working throughout, the billing reads included. Show `Exception.Message` and [Action](#errors.BillingPaymentRequiredException.Action) to a person; once paid, send the request again (a write under the same idempotency key). Execution methods never throw: an order refused for billing comes back as a refused [ExecutionResult](#execution.ExecutionResult) whose [ExecutionResult.Detail](#execution.ExecutionResult.Detail) carries this error's text. The error's `cause` is [BillingCause](#errors.BillingPaymentRequiredException.BillingCause) here, so it cannot be read as an exception's own cause (`Exception.InnerException`).
